extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers (PIs), institutional research administrators, and policy/portfolio analysts interested in NIGMS R01/MIRA funding trends
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and interpret NIGMS investigator- and award-level metrics (R01 and R01-equivalent/MIRA) across fiscal years to inform investigators and administrators about application, award, and demographic trends. Includes methods for constructing comparator groups and privacy-aware reporting practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of PIs who held more than one NIGMS R01
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure 1 shows the percentage of PIs who held more than one NIGMS R01 between fiscal years 2014 and 2024 (FY14 and FY24). In FY14 and FY15, only 16% of PIs had more than one NIGMS R01. This percentage hovered around 14-15% until 2019, when it began declining.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation guidance provided: the decline was likely the result of an increasing number of PIs converting their R01s to MIRAs and an Institute policy that PIs could not have more than two NIGMS R01s. Note that even before MIRA, only a small fraction of PIs had more than one NIGMS R01; compare to prior analyses of second-R01 acquisition among ESIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIRA investigator effort and NIGMS ineligibility rule
rubrics_metrics.description: MIRA investigators must dedicate 51% of their research effort toward the grant and are ineligible to apply for or receive other NIGMS research support (with some exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit program requirement is used to explain post-award applicant/funding behavior and constraints (e.g., lower likelihood of holding multiple NIGMS awards). Use when comparing application patterns between MIRA and R01 awardees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative investigator rate
rubrics_metrics.description: At NIGMS, we focus on supporting a broad group of investigators. As a result, we monitor two statistics that describe our investigator pool: the cumulative investigator rate and the number of funded early stage investigators (ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cumulative investigator rate is tracked as a high-level statistic describing the makeup of funded investigators; use alongside ESI counts to evaluate breadth and distribution of support over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of funded Early Stage Investigators (ESIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figure 1 illustrates the number of ESIs who received their first competing NIGMS R01-equivalent grants each year between FY2013 and FY2022. In FY2022, NIGMS awarded R01-equivalent grants to 319 ESIs in total: 31 investigators received R01 awards, 268 investigators received R35 (MIRA) awards, and 20 investigators received NIH Director’s New Innovator Awards (DP2s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count ESIs by award type; include DP2s administered by NIGMS where relevant. Use year-to-year trends (rises/falls) and note program introductions (e.g., MIRA in FY2016) that alter applicant pools. Report yearly direct counts and contextual explanations for changes (e.g., built-up applicant pool exhaustion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award rates (percentage of reviewed applications that receive funding)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first section, we present award rates (the percentage of reviewed applications that receive funding), considering both programs overall and then FY2021 renewal applications specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare award rates across programs (MIRA vs R01), and across investigator types (Established Investigators vs Early Stage Investigators). Where sample sizes and privacy concerns allow, report subgroup rates. Use award rates to evaluate competitiveness and program outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award sizes and yearly direct costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The second section describes the award sizes for the two types of grants collectively, followed by award size changes for FY2021 renewals. All budget values shown in the post are yearly direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report award sizes in yearly direct costs and analyze changes across renewals and conversions (e.g., converting R01s to MIRAs). Use award-size comparisons to infer resource implications of program choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative analysis of MIRA renewals vs R01 renewals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIGMS funded its first round of renewals for the MIRA program in Fiscal Year (FY) 2021. In this post, we compare data on the award rates and award sizes of MIRA renewals and R01 renewals to provide some insights into the early outcomes of MIRA renewals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing renewals, consider award rates and award-size changes, and stratify results by investigator career stage (EIs vs ex-ESIs) where possible. Use caution with small sample sizes and privacy constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant demographic reporting and privacy practices
rubrics_metrics.description: We look at trends for applicants by race/ethnicity and by gender. Due to privacy requirements and small numbers, applicants from underrepresented racial and ethnic groups in biomedical research (Black or African American, Hispanic or Latino, American Indian or Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian and other Pacific Islander) are combined into a larger group that can be reported. Because of the small applicant numbers, we’re unable to show intersectional analyses of race/ethnicity and gender or analyses of applicants with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow privacy-aware aggregation rules when reporting demographic breakdowns; be explicit when aggregation prevents intersectional analyses. Note limitations in interpretability due to small subgroup sample sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of comparator groups for program comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: To compare application behavior between MIRA and R01-funded investigators, we created sets of both established (EI) and early stage (ESI) investigators supported by NIGMS R01s (called the comparator group) who have not received a MIRA. The EI comparators were matched according to race/ethnicity, gender, time since acquisition of first R01, and average annual NIGMS funding. For the ESI comparator group, we used all ESI NIGMS R01 awardees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use matched comparator groups controlling for demographics, career timing, and historical funding levels to isolate program effects. Document matching variables and inclusion criteria; state any deviations or limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring investigator-level trends for competing R01/R01-equivalent RPGs
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of its commitment to transparency, NIGMS examines and publishes data on annual trends reflected in its RPG portfolio. In this post, we review and describe investigator-level trends associated with competing R01/R01-equivalent RPGs including those in the Institute’s R35 MIRA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report investigator-level trends (applications, awards, renewals) annually and contextualize within Institute mission (supporting a broad range of topics and investigators). Use longitudinal figures and tables to show temporal patterns and program impacts.
